title: Nia and the Shape Surprise
markdown:
The late afternoon sun lay like a warm blanket across the meadow. Nia’s fingers still held the whisper of soil from planting tiny seeds. She hummed. Dr. Sol, kind eyes, voice like warm milk, held a special parcel for Science Club. Wisp, her fluffy ginger cat, purred a rumbling lullaby.

Sol’s voice was soft as falling snow. He held a bundle tied with gentle string. “For Sorting.”

It opened: flat colourful pieces, smooth as quiet pebbles; others like playful party hats. Mixed in, solid shapes — round and warm for rolling, sturdy cubes for building, soft pyramids like tiny tents.

Nia’s brow creased. “So many. How will we sort them?” A fleeting overwhelm made her toes wiggle.

Sol knelt, calming as a breeze, and left the dear-Nia aside. “A puzzle. Look closely.” A flat soft blue circle. “Like a drawing on paper. Two-dimensional. 2D.” A round red ball rolled in his palm. “Roundness you can hold all around. Three-dimensional. 3D.”

Wisp blinked slowly, tail a soft flick. Nia looked from the quiet circle on the table to the warm ball. A picture. A thing you could hold.

“Flat ones 2D. Ones we can hold, 3D.”

“Precisely.” Sol’s eyes twinkled.

The worry melted. She picked up a flat yellow square. “Smooth.” A neat pile. A solid red cube. “Sides all around. Strong. 3D.” A separate pile. Wisp watched from her perch, bright eyes following.

Soon the rhythm was a gentle dance. Flat triangles and circles, rectangles and ovals — 2D, peaceful. Then spheres, cubes, cones, prisms — 3D, satisfying to stack. The bundle emptied into two honest groups.

“You’ve solved it.”

Nia felt the sun-warmth of having finished. Two piles: quiet flats, comforting solids. Sol did not offer a key to buildings and stars. He let the piles sit.

Nia looked at her hands, which now knew the difference, and yawned a cozy yawn into Wisp’s fur. The world of shapes did not need to unfold like moonlight. The parcel string, coiled, was ready for the next club if anyone brought another jumble.
